title: Verification of Unknown Dynamical Systems via Autoencoder Latent Space
abstract: arXiv:2512.13593v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Formal verification provides a powerful framework for proving that dynamical systems satisfy their specifications. However, these techniques face scalability challenges in high-dimensional settings, as they often rely on state-space discretization which grows exponentially with dimension. Learning-based approaches to dimensionality reduction have shown great potential to alleviate this problem. However, ensuring correctness of latent space verification results remains an open question. In this work, we provide a formal approach to reduce the dimensionality of systems via convex autoencoders and learn the dynamics in the latent space through a kernel-based method. We then construct a finite abstraction from the learned model in the latent space and guarantee that the abstraction contains the true behaviors of the original system. We show that the verification results in the latent space can be mapped back to the original system. Final

translated_title: 基于自编码器潜在空间的未知动力系统验证
translated_abstract: 形式化验证为证明动力系统满足其规约提供了强大的框架。然而，这些技术在高维场景下面临可扩展性挑战，因为它们通常依赖于随维度呈指数级增长的状态空间离散化。基于学习的降维方法在缓解这一问题上展现出巨大潜力，但如何确保潜在空间验证结果的正确性仍是一个悬而未决的问题。在本工作中，我们提供了一种通过凸自编码器对系统进行降维的形式化方法，并通过基于核的方法在潜在空间中学习系统动力学。随后，我们从潜在空间中学到的模型构建有限抽象，并保证该抽象包含原始系统的真实行为。我们证明了在潜在空间中得到的验证结果可以映射回原始系统。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种通过凸自编码器降维并利用基于核的方法在潜在空间中学习动力学的形式化验证框架，保证了所构建的有限抽象包含原系统的真实行为，并可将潜在空间中的验证结果映射回原始系统。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a formal verification framework that reduces dimensionality via convex autoencoders and learns dynamics in latent space through kernel-based methods, guaranteeing that the constructed finite abstraction contains the true behaviors of the original system and that latent-space verification results can be mapped back to it.
